observed_title: Simultaneous Pointwise Majorization for Mixed Tail Processes with Applications in Gaussian Chaos and Ergodic Diffusions
version: arXiv:2609.01576v2, 46 PDF pages (version/date details not independently checked beyond the first-page arXiv identifier).

read_ranges.scope: 全文逐行阅读：引言、mixed-tail setup、Theorems 2.1/3.1、diffusion and Gaussian-chaos applications、Appendices A–E including the complete theorem/application proofs, discussion and references。

topic_relevance.K03: direct. Theorem 3.1 proves simultaneous all-index pointwise majorization for a separable Banach-valued process with finitely many genuinely mixed-tail increment geometries. The proof uses measure-generated admissible chains, a nested common refinement across metrics, and a countable dense-set passage to a single all-t event. The article also derives decoupled Gaussian-chaos and stationary-diffusion applications. It does not claim constants uniform in the number of regimes.

definitions.name: finite-regime mixed-tail process
definitions.statement: A separable Banach space B and standard Borel index space (T,A); finite-valued jointly measurable pseudometrics d_j, orders α_j>0, and separable ρ=Σ_j d_j. A jointly measurable process has a modification whose paths are ρ-continuous and which is anchored at t0. For every s,t and common u≥0, P{||Z_t−Z_s||>Σ_j u^(1/α_j)d_j(s,t)}≤2e^(−u). This is one joint mixed-tail inequality; it is not m separately assumed single-metric inequalities, and no process decomposition is assumed.

definitions.name: pointwise Fernique–Talagrand profile
definitions.statement: For fixed Borel probability measures µ_j selected before observing the process, v_j(t)=d_j(t,t0), Φ_j(t)=∫_0^{4v_j(t)}[log(1/µ_j(B_{d_j}(t,r)))]^(1/α_j)dr, with closed balls and the integral interpreted in the extended-real sense (log(1/0)=∞).

definitions.name: partition norms for decoupled Gaussian chaos
definitions.statement: For a q-tensor A and partition P of [q], ||A||_P is the supremum of the multilinear contraction over one unit-Euclidean-norm test array per block. The one-block norm is Frobenius; the q-singleton norm is the injective norm. The application scales d_P(s,t)=K_q||A_s−A_t||_P and uses order α_P=2/|P|.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.1 (multi-regime pointwise majorization)
assumptions: B is a separable Banach space; (T,A) is standard Borel; the finite-valued jointly measurable pseudometrics d_j have separable sum ρ and orders α_j>0.
The process is jointly measurable and has a modification whose ρ-paths are continuous and which is anchored at t0 almost surely.
For all s,t and all u≥0, the common-parameter mixed-tail inequality P{||Z_t−Z_s||>Σ_j u^(1/α_j)d_j(s,t)}≤2e^(−u) holds.
Each ambient Borel probability µ_j is fixed before observing the process.
theorem_cards.statement: There is a finite C_{m,α}, depending only on m and the orders α, such that for each δ∈(0,1), with probability at least 1−δ, simultaneously for every t∈T, ||Z_t||≤C_{m,α} Σ_{j=1}^m [Φ_j(t)+v_j(t)(log(e/δ))^(1/α_j)]. If a Φ_j(t) is infinite, the bound there is vacuous.
proof_steps: Finite K: Lemma C.3 builds, for each regime j, an admissible chain T_{j,k} whose pointwise weighted chain cost is at most C^(1)_{α_j}(Φ_j(t)+v_j(t)); the construction uses greedy mass-radius nets and summation by parts. Source lines 1750–1862, PDF pp.30–32.

Synchronize the chains by recording all nearest-net labels through level n−b_m, where b_m=1+ceil(log_2 m); the nested refinement has at most 2^(2^n) cells. Choose one representative per cell minimizing the combined weighted approximation cost, telescope common parent-child edges, union-bound their mixed-tail increments, and retain explicit constants depending on m and α. Lemma C.4, source lines 1863–2106, PDF pp.32–36.
Substitute the measure-chain costs in the finite-set estimate to obtain Lemma C.5, probability at least 1−e^(−u) simultaneously on each finite K. Source lines 2107–2147, PDF pp.36–37.

For full T, use Borel rational upper-level sets H_{q,s}={Φ_j≤q_j,v_j≤s_j}, select countable ρ-dense subsets, intersect the decreasing finite-set events, extend via path continuity, and let rational q_j,s_j decrease to Φ_j(t),v_j(t). The common event is independent of t. Source lines 2148–2220, PDF pp.37–39.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Appendix C.4: nested common refinement and finite-set mixed-tail telescope.
Appendix C.5 and proof of Theorem 3.1: finite-to-full separable index space passage.

gaps: The article states a finite constant and supplies explicit proof dependence on m and α, but does not claim or establish a bound uniform in m.
Prior measures are fixed before process observation. Reusing the result with data-selected priors, metrics or anchors needs a separate conditioning/sample-splitting argument.
The all-t extension applies to the stipulated continuous modification and the stated separability/Borel hypotheses; it is not a measurability-free supremum assertion.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma C.4–C.5 (finite common-refinement estimate)
assumptions: K is finite and contains t0; each regime has an admissible sequence anchored at {t0} and eventually equal to K.
The process satisfies the same m-regime mixed-tail increment condition.
theorem_cards.statement: For every u≥1, with probability at least 1−e^(−u), simultaneously for t∈K, ||Z_t||≤B_{m,α}Σ_j[Φ_j(t)+u^(1/α_j)v_j(t)] after choosing the measure-generated chains from Lemma C.3. Lemma C.4 first bounds the process by the chain costs G_j(t)=Σ_k2^(k/α_j)d_j(t,T_{j,k}) plus the anchor confidence costs.
proof_steps: Define equivalence classes from the joint labels p_{j,k}(t) at all j and levels k≤n−b_m. By |T_{j,k}|≤2^(2^k), the cell count satisfies ∏_{j=1}^m∏_{k=0}^{n−b_m}|T_{j,k}|≤∏_{j=1}^m∏_{k=0}^{n−b_m}2^(2^k)=2^(m(2^(n−b_m+1)−1))≤2^(2^n), using m≤2^(b_m−1) (PDF p.33, (C.10)).
Choose the representative minimizing R_n(t)=Σ_j2^(n/α_j)d_j(t,T_{j,n−b_m}); common labels and triangle inequalities bound parent-child edge lengths by R_n and R_{n−1}.

Union-bound coarse edges at level floor(log_2 u) and finer edges at levels n with deviation parameters 16u and 16·2^n. Sum the resulting exponential tails to at most e^(−u), then telescope until the finite chains reach t.
Apply the deterministic mass-chain estimate and absorb v_j into u^(1/α_j)v_j since u≥1.
gaps: This finite chaining proof presumes the supplied measure-generated admissible chains and finite index set. The extension to arbitrary T is a separate countable-density/continuity argument in Theorem 3.1.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.3 (decoupled Gaussian chaos application)
assumptions: q≥2; g^(1),…,g^(q) are independent standard Gaussian vectors; T is standard Borel; t↦A_t is a Borel map into a finite-dimensional tensor space and A_{t0}=0.
For each partition P of [q], d_P(s,t)=K_q||A_s−A_t||_P and α_P=2/|P|, where K_q=e^(2qL_q) and L_q is the constant in cited Lemma A.5.
theorem_cards.statement: Proposition 5.2 verifies finite jointly Borel pseudometrics, separability, joint measurability and almost-sure ρ-continuity, and proves the common mixed-tail increment condition. Theorem 5.3 then yields, with probability at least 1−δ simultaneously for all t, |C_t^(q)|≤C_q Σ_{P∈P_q}[Φ_P(t)+v_P(t)(log(e/δ))^(|P|/2)], where C_q depends only on q. For fixed q, the authors state an analogous envelope for diagonal-free coupled chaos via a cited decoupling inequality, with q-dependent factors.
proof_steps: For u>log 2, take p=max(2,u), so p≤4u; apply the cited Latala partition-norm moment inequality to the increment tensor, absorb powers into K_q, and use Markov at e times the Lp norm to get the common mixed-tail event. For u≤log 2 the right side of the tail bound is at least one.

Use ||A||_P≤||A||_F and the one-block Frobenius norm to show ρ is equivalent to the finite-dimensional Frobenius metric on the image {A_t}, hence separable; the finite-sum chaos representation yields joint measurability and a.s. ρ-Lipschitz paths.

Apply Theorem 3.1 to the B_q regimes. The printed theorem statement and its absolute-value sign were checked visually on PDF p.13; the increment inequality and moment-to-tail calculation were checked visually on PDF p.42, and the norm/separability argument on pp.43–44.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Appendix E: complete proof of Proposition 5.2, Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.4.

gaps: The Latala moment inequality (Lemma A.5) and the diagonal-free decoupling result are cited inputs; this reading checked the paper’s stated application/reduction but did not independently prove those external results.
The constant depends on q through the moment constant, K_q and Theorem 3.1’s regime count; the source does not give a q-uniform bound.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4 (stationary diffusion occupation process)
assumptions: Assumptions 4.1–4.2: a stationary one-dimensional diffusion with globally Lipschitz coefficients and a dissipative tail condition as specified in the article; F is standard Borel, consists of bounded Borel functions, contains 0, has jointly Borel evaluation, jointly Borel d1,d2, and is separable under d1.
The trajectory is started from the invariant distribution π; τ>0; ambient priors µ1,µ2 are fixed before observing the trajectory.
theorem_cards.statement: The occupation process is an anchored two-metric mixed-tail process of orders (1,2), with d1(f,h)=sqrt(C_P/τ)|| (f−h)−π(f−h)||∞ and d2(f,h)=sqrt(2)V_π(f−h), where V_π is the long-run variance seminorm defined in the article. Theorem 2.1 yields one event of probability at least 1−δ on which the pointwise occupation bound holds simultaneously for every f, with local profiles Φ1,Φ2 and radius penalties v1 log(e/δ), v2 sqrt(log(e/δ)).
proof_steps: Appendix D establishes finiteness/seminorm properties of V_π, identifies it with the asymptotic variance by a CLT plus uniform integrability, and uses the Poincaré inequality to obtain the mixed-tail increment inequality.

Joint Borel evaluation and parametrized integration give joint measurability; a uniform-norm increment estimate gives sample-path continuity. Proposition 4.3 verifies the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, after which the pointwise profile and confidence terms substitute directly.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Appendix D proofs of Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4; PDF pp.41–42.

gaps: The Poincaré, diffusion concentration and CLT inputs are reduced to cited results/lemmas; this card records the article’s derivation, not independent validation of those external theorems.
This is an application for the stated stationary scalar diffusion/function-class assumptions, not a general Markov-process concentration theorem.

constant_dependence.explicit: Theorem 3.1 gives C_{m,α} depending only on m and the orders α_j. In the proof b_m=1+ceil(log_2 m), the finite-set common-refinement factor includes max_j 2^(b_m/α_j), and the remaining factors depend on α; C_{m,α} is not asserted uniform in m. The chaos application adds q-dependence through L_q, K_q and the Bell number B_q of regimes.
constant_dependence.applications: Diffusion uses the universal two-regime constant C_{1,2}; its increment metrics contain the Poincaré constant C_P and time τ. No new independent numerical estimate for C_{1,2} is supplied.

endpoint_limits.complexity: Profiles are extended-real; any infinite Φ_j makes the indexwise bound vacuous.
endpoint_limits.localization: The integral ends at 4v_j(t), so only anchor-comparable scales enter. If v_j(t)=0, the corresponding profile is zero.
endpoint_limits.priors: Each µ_j must be fixed before observing the process; data-adaptive priors are not directly covered.
endpoint_limits.regime_count: Finite m only; constant grows through an explicit but not claimed sharp dependence on m and α.

reusable_methods.method: Synchronize finitely many metric-specific mass chains by a nested refinement that records all regime labels through shifted levels.
reusable_methods.transfer: For another process with one common mixed-tail increment inequality and finitely many metrics, reproduce the level-count and parent-child edge argument; verify tail calibration and whether all priors can be fixed independently.

reusable_methods.method: Pass from finite subsets to a common all-index event via rational upper-level sets of deterministic envelopes, countable dense subsets, decreasing finite-set events and sample continuity.
reusable_methods.transfer: Transfer requires Borel profiles, separability of the relevant pseudometric quotient, and a continuous modification; these are substantive hypotheses, not automatic from separable terminology.

reusable_methods.method: Convert a finite-dimensional tensor-chaos moment estimate into a mixed-tail increment condition by choosing p=max(2,u), comparing p with u, and Markov at e times the Lp scale.
reusable_methods.transfer: The moment estimate and all constants must be verified for the target chaos; this application uses decoupled Gaussian inputs and Latala partition norms.

unchecked: Entire extracted 46-page article was read (paper.md lines 1–2688). Major formulas in the main theorem (PDF p.8), common-refinement proof (pp.33–40), chaos application (p.13) and its proofs (pp.42–44) were visually checked using PyMuPDF renders.

Full reading is not an independent proof certification. In particular the article relies on cited generic chaining/majorizing measure, Poincaré, diffusion concentration, CLT, Latala moment and decoupling results; their external proofs were not independently rechecked.
